spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation: The Three Coverings of External Truth

---

## ¶1

When the living Divine influx descended from the Lord, it bore with it three coverings of external truth: the truth of rational understanding, the truth of love's activity, and the truth of natural knowledge. The Divine appropriated these coverings from [GAP-1] the celestial origin; it [GAP-2] clothed itself within them, within those three external truths, [GAP-3] so that the Divine might operate through successive degrees. It set into Divine order [GAP-4: REVIEW — these truths as governing forms] for all states of existence both interior and exterior, celestial and natural. It disposed them according to [GAP-5] the form through which the Divine was made manifest. Thereafter, [GAP-6] when the Divine purpose was accomplished, its goods of use [GAP-7] and the [GAP-8] interior reality was laid bare — it divested itself of these external coverings before those who live in the good of charity.

## ¶2

Now, when the Divine influx was about to release [GAP-9: these external truths from their fixed containment, it] separated itself from them by dissolving their binding conjunction, and it [GAP-10: withdrew its presence from] within them, and thus these three coverings of external truth are disposed in order [GAP-11] extending from beneath the outermost boundary of the containing sphere, inasmuch as they encompass all states [GAP-12] ascending [GAP-13] toward what is interior [GAP-14] ascending [GAP-15] — what is inmost and above them strips away the containing boundary from its highest and most interior degree; and what had descended into the lowest natural state is received beneath these coverings and elevated back to the celestial heights from which the Divine had originally proceeded at the very beginning of all influx.

---

### Interpretive Note

The chapter describes a complete arc of Divine operation: the Lord clothes Himself in successive external truths — rational thought, love's warmth, factual knowledge — in order to establish order through all degrees of creation. Having accomplished this ordering, He reveals the interior Divine reality to the regenerate by removing the external coverings. The "zone" (containing boundary) corresponds to the limiting sphere that separates interior states from exterior — what Swedenborg calls the *limbus* or boundary between the spiritual and natural degrees. The garments descend so that all things may be set in order; then they are removed and what had descended is elevated back to its celestial origin, completing the circuit of influx and return that constitutes all Divine providence in created states.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: when the Living Spirit came he brought the three garments; that of wind, that of fire, and that of water. He assumed them from [the heights] he has [clothed himself] in them in those three garments [and through them] he established [them] for all the things of [this univers]e, both above and below. He arranged them in the [form in which] he was displayed. Afterwards [he completed] his works [and] the [image was revealed, and]e stripped them off before [the ri]ghteous ones.

Now, when he was about to loose [and release them,] divested himself of them from their (clasp) and he [was no more]n them, and thus these three g[arme]nts are arranged [and extend] from below the edges of the zone as they clothe i[t al]l [reaching] up [to what is] above [and reaching] up [to what is] above them strips them of the zone from that place at its topmost point; and it is placed below them and ra[ised u]p to the heights above, from which it had been sent o[u]t at their beginning.

fills.explanation: The spiritual reading says "the celestial origin," and the passage's closing line says the garments return "to the heights above, from which it had been sent out at their beginning" — creating an inclusio with "He assumed them from the heights."
The spiritual reading says "clothed itself within them" and the context of assuming garments requires the reflexive verb of putting them on: "he has clothed himself in them."

The spiritual reading says "so that the Divine might operate through successive degrees," indicating the garments are the means of operation; "and through them he established" captures this instrumental sense in the Kephalaia's register.
The editor's "them" correctly refers to the three garments/truths that the Living Spirit set in order for all things of the universe; the spiritual reading confirms "these truths as governing forms."

The spiritual reading says "the form through which the Divine was made manifest"; the natural text requires "He arranged them in the form in which he was displayed," describing the garments ordered according to the Divine's manifest form.

The spiritual reading says "when the Divine purpose was accomplished," and the natural text requires "Afterwards he completed his works" to introduce the transition from establishing order to removing the garments.

The spiritual reading shows a conjunction between "its goods of use" and "the interior reality was laid bare"; the simple conjunction "and" connects "his works" to the next clause about the image being revealed.

The spiritual reading says "interior reality was laid bare — it divested itself"; in Manichaean vocabulary the divine "image" (eikōn) is the interior reality, and the fill connects to "he" (h visible in gap + e outside) to give "the image was revealed, and he stripped them off."

The spiritual reading says "these external truths from their fixed containment"; the fill bridges "loosen them" to "he divested himself," with "and release them" describing the act of freeing the garments from their bound state before the full divesting from the clasp.

The spiritual reading says "withdrew its presence from within them"; "he was no more in them" expresses the Divine presence departing from the garments after divesting, with the fill connecting to the visible "i" and "n" to form "in."

The spiritual reading says "extending from beneath the outermost boundary"; "are arranged and extend from below the edges of the zone" describes the garments stretching from the lowest boundary upward.
The spiritual reading says "ascending" at this point; "reaching up" in the natural register describes the garments extending upward from where they clothe all things toward the higher degrees.

The spiritual reading says "toward what is interior"; "up to what is above" in the natural register describes the garments reaching toward the higher degree, where "above" corresponds to "interior" in the doctrine of correspondences.
The spiritual reading says "ascending" again at this second stage; "and reaching up" parallels GAP-12 in the repeated ascending pattern, describing the garments extending to the next higher degree.

The spiritual reading says "what is inmost and above them"; "up to what is above them" identifies the inmost Divine reality that transcends all three garments and acts as the subject that "strips them of the zone from that place at its topmost point."
